headline: Remote Lodge and Bear Viewing Access
reservation: Book Brooks Camp Campground through Recreation.gov using the current annual release schedule; it is separate from Brooks Lodge reservations and transportation bookings. For 2026, campground nights are released in three blocks on January 7, February 7 and March 7 at 8 AM Alaska Standard Time. Check NPS for future-year dates and current bear-management rules.

days.title: Brown Bear Observation

stops.name: Brooks Falls Platform
stops.detail: Watch brown bears fish for salmon from the safety of elevated boardwalks managed by park rangers.

stops.name: Brooks River Lower Platform
stops.detail: Observe bears and cubs in the slower waters near the mouth of the river.

days.driving: Walking only within Brooks Camp; floatplane arrival from King Salmon is required
days.note: Bear jams can delay walking between platforms; allow extra time for all movements.

days.title: Volcanic History

stops.name: Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes
stops.detail: Take the official bus tour to witness the site of the 1912 Novarupta eruption.

stops.name: Three Forks Overlook
stops.detail: View the vast ash-filled valley and the Ukak River gorge from this high vantage point.

days.driving: Allow about 7 hours for the guided Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes bus excursion, including stops and the optional hike; reserve in advance.
days.note: The bus tour is weather-dependent and requires advance booking.

days.title: Cultural and Lake Exploration
days.start: Suggested: 10:00 AM from Brooks Camp Visitor Center

stops.name: Reconstructed Alutiiq/Sugpiaq Home
stops.detail: Follow the cultural trail to a reconstructed traditional Alutiiq/Sugpiaq home to learn about the human history of Brooks River.

stops.name: Naknek Lake Shoreline
stops.detail: Walk the designated beach areas for views of the surrounding Aleutian Range peaks.

days.driving: Local transfer by air or water; allow 30 minutes for floatplane staging
days.note: Stay alert for bears even in the camp vicinity; always follow ranger safety guidelines.

intel.title: Air Taxi Staging
intel.text: There are no car parking lots; floatplanes dock at the Naknek Lake beach. Visitors must clear all gear from the landing area immediately upon arrival.

intel.title: Communication Realities
intel.text: Cellular and Wi-Fi services are effectively non-existent in the park. Handheld satellite devices are recommended for those venturing into the backcountry.

intel.title: Supplies and Calories
intel.text: There are no grocery stores or gas stations in the park. All food must be purchased at the lodge or brought in bear-resistant containers.

intel.title: Platform Waiting Lists
intel.text: During peak July salmon runs, the Falls Platform uses a pager system with wait times up to several hours. Plan to spend time at the lower platforms or visitor center while waiting.

intel.title: Mandatory Orientation
intel.text: All visitors must attend 'Bear School' at the visitor center immediately upon landing. You will not be permitted to access the trails or platforms without this safety briefing.

plan.arrival: Fly into King Salmon (AKN) then transfer to a floatplane; check in for Bear School immediately upon landing at Brooks Camp.
plan.vehicle: No road access for cars or RVs; travel is strictly by aircraft, boat, or foot within camp boundaries.
plan.goldenHour: Dusk at the Brooks River mouth offers sightings of bears, though visibility depends on summer cloud cover.
